summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability and crash-resume soundness) of the CipherBox GSD workflow, expanding scope twice mid-planning (Rust engine.rs twin, then desktop FUSE RotationDeps live-wiring) and finally executing all 13 resulting plans across 7 waves using parallel git worktrees.
summary.outcome: Phase 70.1 was fully planned (13 PLAN.md files, plan-checker passed, 17/17 decision coverage) and executed through Wave 4 merged (9 of 13 plans landed, including a mid-wave SDK hoist of IndexedDB logic for CI coverage and the production RotationDeps adapter); Waves 5-7 (gate fixes, test inversion, desktop-e2e human checkpoint) remained to be executed.

repo: Decision-coverage gate parser (.claude/gsd-core/bin/lib/decisions.cjs) only accepts D-NN bullets in three exact forms (`- **D-NN:**`, `- **D-NN — title**`, `- **D-NN: Title.**`); a period-before-closing-`**` form silently breaks parsing for ALL bullets in the file, not just the malformed one.

state.planned-phase and similarly-named STATE.md update tools can silently no-op (`updated: []`) if STATE.md's structure doesn't match their expected anchors — must verify with a follow-up read, not trust the echoed success.
gsd commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative when lint-staged actually completes successfully — verify via `git log`/`git status` rather than retrying.
render-hooks --raw JSON output can contain literal newlines making it invalid JSON; read the hook file directly instead of parsing --raw output.

crates/fuse/src/write_ops/grant_scope.rs's rotate_read_on_scope_exit was a documented 'LIVE-WIRING RESIDUAL' stub returning Err (fails closed/EIO) because the only impl RotationDeps in the workspace was the test FakeDeps — this was tracked by an orphaned pending todo not claimed by any outlined phase.

Rust rotate engine (crates/sdk/src/rotation/engine.rs) is a structural twin of TS packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/engine.ts but was naiver: non-recursive verify_subtree_clean, missing-root treated as clean, DirtyFrontierEntry missing parent_ipns_name/node_read_key fields, and republish_parent lacking the TS twin's CAS-409 merge-retry.

publish_ipns's PublishResult::Conflict only returns current_sequence_number, not the full PublishedNode, so a RotationDeps adapter needing PublishAttempt::Conflict's `remote` field must do an extra resolve+fetch round-trip (easy to miss, silently breaks concurrent-add merge).

SentSharesCache fail-open bug: an unrefreshed/empty cache is treated as 'private, no rotation needed' — fix must key on 'successfully refreshed once' not 'set is non-empty', else legitimate zero-share private deletes break.

Running cargo fmt --all (unscoped) inside a plan's worktree reformats unrelated out-of-scope files as uncommitted drift that blocks cleanup-wave merges with worktree_dirty; scoping to `cargo fmt -p <crate>` avoids this.

Cross-package dist staleness is a real trap: after Wave 2 changed sdk-core (packages/sdk-core), the sdk package's vitest suite ran against a stale pre-change dist, producing 3 false-failing tests until dists were rebuilt in dependency order (crypto→core→api-client→sdk-core→sdk).

code.finding: verify_subtree_clean was non-recursive and treated a missing root record as clean (not dirty) before Plan 04's fix; this masked crash-resume soundness bugs.

rotate_read_on_scope_exit returned Err(RotationError::RotateFailed(...)) unconditionally — the only RotationDeps impl in the workspace was the test FakeDeps, so desktop FUSE rotation always failed closed until Plan 09 wired FuseRotationDeps.
Post-merge of Wave 4 left an unused `NodeKind` import (merge artifact from combined 03/09 edits to fs.rs), cleaned up manually since CI doesn't use -D warnings but reviewers flag it.

workflow: When a user asks for 'independent worktrees for concurrent plans,' dispatch worktree-creation agent calls one-per-message (not batched) to avoid simultaneous `git worktree add` calls racing on .git/config.lock; once created, the agents run truly concurrently.

Running a single plan first as a synchronous 'canary' to validate the worktree→commit→SUMMARY→merge pipeline before fanning out to the full wave is a reasonable risk-mitigation, but should be explicitly communicated to the user rather than assumed — the user pushed back when only 1 of 4 expected concurrent plans appeared to be running.
After merging a wave, always rebuild all affected package dists before running downstream post-merge test gates that consume those packages as dependencies, or false regressions appear.

When a subagent's returned <worktree_metadata> expected_base looks wrong (e.g., equals its own final commit instead of the true fork base), don't trust it blindly — verify against the actual wave base captured before dispatch.

Deferring a live e2e/docker-dependent test run from a worktree subagent to the orchestrator (scoping the subagent to 'write + typecheck only') is a valid pattern for infra-constrained test suites — keeps subagents parallel while centralizing flaky/infra-heavy verification.

friction: Decision-coverage gate failure message ('0/15 covered, malformed bullets') didn't identify which bullet was malformed, requiring manual regex-testing of every D-NN bullet against the parser's three accepted forms to find the D-09/D-10 offenders.
state.planned-phase tool silently no-op'd instead of erroring, requiring a manual STATE.md edit and an extra verification round-trip to catch it.
gsd commit helper's false-negative failure report required an extra git log check to confirm the commit actually landed.

cleanup-wave merge helper blocked on Plan 03's worktree due to unscoped cargo fmt --all drift across 13 unrelated files, requiring manual diff inspection to confirm it was pure formatting before discarding.
Post-merge test failures for Wave 3 (3 failing tests in client-rotation.test.ts) turned out to be stale sdk-core dist rather than a real regression, costing an investigation cycle.
The user pushed back mid-execution ('why is only 1 plan of wave 1 executing?'), indicating the canary-first strategy wasn't communicated clearly enough before starting.
open_items: Waves 5, 6, and 7 of Phase 70.1 still need execution: Wave 5 (Plan 11, gate-fix authoritativeness/ancestor/poisoned-lock), Wave 6 (Plan 12, gate ordering + dest_ino + test inversion of delete.rs:644), Wave 7 (Plan 13, desktop-e2e human-checkpoint acceptance, autonomous:false).
Final gsd-verifier goal-backward verification pass and STATE/ROADMAP updates for the full phase are still pending until all waves complete.

ROT-04 (desktop grant re-mint via query_grants_rooted_at/update_grant/delete_grant) was deliberately deferred as trait no-ops in Plan 09 — inner sub-share re-mint is not enforced on the desktop path; documented as a sanctioned scope decision but remains a known limitation.

IPNS signing-key sourcing from the local InodeTable with fail-closed behavior for non-materialized nodes was a gap RESEARCH didn't specify a source for; Plan 09 made a documented decision but this may need future revisiting.
Two dangling worktree-agent-* branches from a prior crashed session were noted but not cleaned up; deferred to a sweep at phase end.
Cosmetic heading inconsistency in Plan 01 ('Artifacts this phase produces (master index)' vs '...this plan produces') flagged by plan-checker as non-blocking but never fixed.
